transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Liu, Priya Desai, Maya Chen, Leo Brooks, Alex Rivera, EMEA Sales Observers

Summary:
Quick internal SE/AE enablement focused on standardized messaging, practice demos with common objections (latency vs cost, dedicated vs hosted, security), and competitor positioning. Ran through two short demo segments and gave feedback. Agreed on action items and next steps.

Topics Covered:
- Messaging framework (value props + evidence)
- Demo script: 5-min pitch, 10-min deep demo
- Handling security questions (SOC 2, VPC, KMS)
- Competitive positioning (OpenAI / Anthropic / Bedrock)
- Practical demo tips (batching, caching, quantization mentions)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): alright, uh good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 55 minutes, this is the eighth of the enablement series. Today it's messaging and demo practice, so we'll run two short demos and then open for Q and A, and then action items at the end.
[00:20] Sofia (SE): hey all, quick housekeeping, we're recording, notes will be uploaded to the enablement drive, also small note on the script — keep the first pitch to under five minutes, that's key for scoping motion.
[00:35] Maya (AE): got it. quick question, are we targeting enterprise or mid-market messages for the opening?
[00:40] Jordan (AE): good call — lead with developer-first, then add enterprise controls if it's an enterprise buyer. so start with "fast-to-integrate, predictable inference costs" then layer in dedicated and private options.
[01:05] Leo (SE): i tried saying that yesterday and the prospect asked straight away about private deployment, like, "can you run on-prem?" what's the short answer?
[01:12] Sofia (SE): yes, short answer: we have Redwood Private — VPC and on-prem options, customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. then follow up with decision flow: low-sensitivity -> hosted, regulatory/air-gapped -> private.
[01:30] Jordan (AE): remember to mention the unified API across modes; that's a big differentiator versus some infra vendors that force you to rework client code.
[01:45] Audience: mhmm
[02:00] Ethan (Product): small note, when callers ask about compliance say SOC two and ISO are in progress or "we have SOC 2 type II controls"? we've seen transcription swap, so say "SOC 2" clearly.
[02:15] Maya (AE): ok, demo one is the fast pitch then 5-minute code walk, i'll go first.
[02:25] Demo 1 (Maya): 
[02:26] [Demo start - screen share described]
[02:30] Maya (AE): hi i'm maya, quick pitch — Redwood helps teams ship LLM features with predictable latency and lower cost — we do that by batching, KV caching and smart routing across models/regions. here's an example integrating the Redwood API; you can see the call is a simple POST to /v1/generate, the SDK handles streaming and function calls.
[03:05] Jordan (AE): pause — good, but a nit: when you say "lower cost" give a concrete example, e.g., "autobatching reduced token cost by ~30% on common workloads in our benchmarks", say numbers not just words.
[03:20] Maya (AE): ok noted, add a quick stat.
[03:25] Demo continues with small code sample, some filler and a slightly mis-transcribed term:
[04:10] Maya (AE): so you can pin a model version in the request (we have a model catalog), also you can toggle quantization profiles — we support int8 and other compression to reduce instance footprint.
[04:30] Leo (SE): small thing — buyers often ask about latency — how do we frame dedicated pools vs hosted in terms of SLOs?
[04:40] Sofia (SE): say something like: for most interactive apps Hosted gives lowest friction with competitive latency; for predictable ultra-low p99 latency and throughput you offer Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and SLA-backed targets. mention autoscaling and burst capacity as options.
[05:05] Jordan (AE): roleplay objection: "Your competitor (OpenAI) has bigger models, why pick Redwood?"
[05:14] Ethan (Product): two angles: 1) serving economics & control — Redwood optimizes inference runtime to reduce unit cost and latency, and 2) deployment flexibility — same API across hosted/dedicated/private so customers don't tie themselves to a single cloud model.
[05:35] Audience: mmmh
[05:40] [Timestamp jump]
[12:10] Demo 2 (Leo): targeted technical dive
[12:12] Leo (SE): ok i'm going to demonstrate the Dedicated flow and show an example traffic routing policy that falls back to a cheaper model on high load. so here we have a canary route and an automatic fallback to a quantized variant — note the failover keeps responses online albeit at slightly different latency profile.
[12:45] Jordan (AE): call out cost tradeoffs explicitly — "we'll fall back from high-capacity gpus to a quantized variant with 20% lower throughput but 40% lower cost, so it's a quick way to control spend while avoiding hard outages."
[13:05] Alex (AE): question on caching — prospects often want to know where data is cached and for how long, how do we respond?
[13:12] Sofia (SE): answer: we do prefix/KV caching with configurable TTL, caching can be regional or per-customer depending on privacy controls, and sensitive data can be excluded from caches. if they need no caching, you can disable; if they need persistent caches, talk about Private options.
[13:35] Jordan (AE): also mention audit logs and token-level cost visibility in the Console — customers like the cost breakdown by route and model.
[14:00] [Short side conversation about demo timing and slide order]
[15:10] Audience (EMEA Observer): how do we position versus Bedrock — they say it's integrated with other cloud services which is attractive for customers already on that cloud.
[15:25] Ethan (Product): fair point. Positioning: Bedrock = cloud native model hosting tied to a CSP. Pitch: Redwood = consistent inferencing runtime + control plane independent of cloud, better for multi-cloud or hybrid needs and for teams who want an opinionated serving runtime that reduces per-token cost. Also mention our Optimize toolkit that gives quantization & batching recommendations.
[15:55] Jordan (AE): practical tip: when you get the "we're heavily invested in X cloud" objection, ask whether they need single-vendor simplicity or cross-environment predictability; then map that to Dedicated/Private as needed.
[16:20] Maya (AE): ok quick roleplay, i will be buyer: "We need low latency and can't afford variations. Is hosted safe?"
[16:30] Leo (SE): seller answer: "Hosted is fast to start, and our routing + autoscaling gives good latencies for most cases. For strict p99s choose Dedicated with reserved capacity and SLA."
[17:05] [Crosstalk: small filler, laughter]
[20:00] Security/Compliance segment
[20:05] Jordan (AE): common security checklist items: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), VPC peering, tenant isolation. make sure you know which docs to share: security whitepaper, SOC 2 summary, and architecture diagrams.
[20:30] Sophia (typo in transcript): we noted that sometimes transcript swaps "K M S" or "K V cache" so emphasize the acronym clearly.
[20:50] Alex (AE): question about data residency — buyer wanted EU-only logging, can we support that?
[21:00] Ethan (Product): yes, we can configure region-restricted logging in the Console for enterprise customers, and Private deployments can be fully on-prem. mention that this is typical enterprise ask and should trigger Solutions Eng and Legal loop-in.
[21:30] [Feedback on messaging tone — keep it concise and benefits-first]
[25:00] Demo practice two wrap-up and feedback:
[25:05] Jordan (AE): three quick feedback points for demos — 1) start with problem statement, 2) show one concrete stat or benchmark, 3) end with next-step ask (pilot, benchmark, POC).
[25:25] Maya (AE): got it. I'll update the script.
[26:00] Competitive rebuttals playbook brief:
[26:05] Sofia (SE): we have a short rebuttal list: - OpenAI: "we're focused on serving economics and deployment control"; - Anthropic: "we compete on runtime and predictable cost more than model brand"; - Bedrock: "we provide vendor-agnostic inference and better observability controls". keep rebuttals one-liners.
[28:10] Audience question: what's the best artifact to share after a demo?
[28:18] Jordan (AE): send the competitive one-pager, link to the Quickstart repo, and a short pricing estimate + pilot kickoff template. keep it under 1 page ideally.
[30:00] Practice run: objection handling roleplay
[30:05] Alex (AE): buyer: "We run highly regulated workloads, can you encrypt with our KMS?"
[30:12] Ethan (Product): answer: "Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management in Private and Dedicated (with proper configuration). For Hosted we offer BYOK integrations and customer-managed keys in supported regions."
[31:00] Minor transcription glitches here: buyer name transcribed as "Biyer" occasionally, some punctuation missing, filler words present.
[35:00] Group recap and next steps
[35:10] Jordan (AE): recap: update the demo script, create short videos, finalize the competitive one-pager, and build the FAQ for common compliance asks. owners and due dates listed in action items.
[35:30] Priya (Sales Ops): i'll schedule a follow-up in two weeks to review assets and the recorded vid snippets, calendar invite will be out by end of day.
[36:00] Final Qs: small clarifications on wording and which benchmarks to cite (we said "~30% token cost savings" — use conservative phrasing like "up to ~30% depending on workload").
[37:00] Meeting close: thanks everyone, recording and notes will be in the enablement drive.
[37:10] [END RECORDING]
